description.describe_ch: In Calculus II, there are eight themes covered. First (Integration), more techniques of integration will be introduced, such as Integration by Parts, Trigonometric Substitution and Partial fractions. Apply those techniques of integration to compute the area of planar regions volumes of solids, etc. Second (Indeterminate form and L'H?pital's Rule), more technologies for the topics of limits of special forms will be introduced to connect the topics of limit and convergence of sequences. Third (Improper Integrals) introduces two types of improper integrals and also can be recognized as a particular test for Series convergence. Fourth (Sequences and Series), the infinite sequences and series will be introduced and tests for series convergence, such as geometric series test, ratio test and p-series test, etc. will be presented. Fifth (Power Series), applies tests of series to exam the absolute convergence of power series and find its interval of convergence. Sixth (Taylor and Maclaurin Series) finds the Taylor and Maclaurin series of some functions, such as exponential function   trigonometric function  , natural logarithmic function   or some rational functions. Seventh (Polar coordinates) introduces the polar coordinate to define the curves in plane/space with a parameter and sketch the graphs of curves. Eighth (Multivariate function and Integration) introduces the definition of multivariate function and Riemann Sum and find the approximation of Integration.
